symbols.name: P
symbols.def: A causal completion whose observed marginal is the law of \(O\).

symbols.name: mu0P
symbols.def: The unique continuous version of \(x\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x,A=0]\).

symbols.name: mu1P

symbols.name: tauP
symbols.def: \(\tau_P(x)=\mu_{1,P}(x)-\mu_{0,P}(x)\), using the continuous versions on the full cube.

symbols.name: vBasis
symbols.def: The fixed Lebesgue-orthonormal tensor Legendre basis of total degree at most \(\lceil\gamma\rceil-1\), in a fixed lexicographic order.

symbols.name: bBasis
symbols.def: On each of the \(M_n^d\) equal half-open cubes, \(b_{M_n}\) is the scaled tensor Legendre basis of total degree at most \(p_{\mathrm{deg}}\), extended by zero off that cube and ordered deterministically; its Lebesgue Gram matrix is the identity.

definitions.name: corrected local moments
definitions.construction: Put \(h=h_n\), \(w_i=h^{-d}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in h[0,1]^d\}\), \(v_i=v(X_i/h)\mathbf 1\{X_i\in h[0,1]^d\}\), and \(b_i=b_{M_n}(X_i/h)\mathbf 1\{X_i\in h[0,1]^d\}\), with every zero-indicator product evaluated before an outside-domain basis value. Define \[\widetilde Q_n=\frac1n\sum_iw_iv_iA_i(A_i-3/8)v_i^{\mathsf T}-\frac1{n(n-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}w_iw_jv_i(A_i-3/8)(b_i^{\mathsf T}b_j)A_jv_j^{\mathsf T},\] \[\widetilde R_n=\frac1n\sum_iw_iv_i(Y_i-1/2)(A_i-3/8)-\frac1{n(n-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}w_iw_jv_i(A_i-3/8)(b_i^{\mathsf T}b_j)(Y_j-1/2).\]

definitions.name: That
definitions.construction: With \(\lambda_0=3/16\), define \[\widehat\tau_n(0)=\begin{cases}0,&s_{\min}(\widetilde Q_n)<\lambda_0/2,\\ \operatorname{clip}_{[-3/4,3/4]}\!\left(v(0)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Q_n^{-1}\widetilde R_n\right),&s_{\min}(\widetilde Q_n)\ge\lambda_0/2.\end{cases}\] The branch rule, half-open cells, basis order, ceiling in \(M_n\), and clipping make this a finite total Borel algorithm on every data set.

definitions.name: ComponentHandle
definitions.construction: Construct \(\mathfrak H_n^{\mathrm{comp}}\) by combining a smooth squared partition of unity at a fine scale with a smooth one-sided localization window, shared Rademacher coefficients, and joint \((A,Y)\)-cell perturbations that cancel after one sign average; condition on \(X_{1:n}\), connect observations whose active frames share a coefficient, factor the mixture over connected components, control each non-singleton component through a mixed amplitude derivative, and sum connected subsets by labeled spanning trees.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), consistency and conditional exchangeability imply \(\tau_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x]\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\). Exact full support and continuity determine a unique version on all of \(\mathcal X\), including \(\tau_P(0)\).
statements.justification: The proposition separates a measure-zero conditional-mean convention from the statistical precision problem.
statements.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE identifies CATE under overlap; the present endpoint formulation additionally records why exact full support and continuity identify the boundary value.
statements.consumer: Users of pointwise CATE methods can interpret the lower bound as loss of precision rather than failure of causal identification.

statements.statement: There is a finite constant \(C<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), such that the total estimator \(\widehat\tau_n(0)\) satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)}\mathbb E_{P_O^{\otimes n}}|\widehat\tau_n(0)-\tau_P(0)|\le C\rho_n\] for every \(n\ge2\). More precisely, with \(\ell_n=h_n/M_n\) and \(K_n\asymp M_n^d\), its risk is at most \(C\{h_n^\gamma+\ell_n^S+(nh_n^d)^{-1/2}+\sqrt{K_n}/(nh_n^d)\}\).
statements.justification: A same-class converse is informative only when paired with a finite estimator that attains the candidate order on every data set.
statements.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE supplies the higher-order upper architecture; this theorem records its exact-known-uniform, one-sided, total finite specialization and does not claim the exponent as a new upper rate.
statements.consumer: The theorem gives an implementable precision benchmark for observational CATE workflows that estimate outcome and propensity regressions.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathfrak H_n^{\mathrm{comp}}\) construct, for every \(n\ge2\), two finite priors supported on \(\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) whose target values are separated by at least \(c\rho_n\) and whose actual fixed-\(n\) product mixtures have squared Hellinger distance at most \(1/4\)? The required certificate must prove exact equality of every singleton conditional mixture, the uniform component inequality \(H^2(Q_{r,+},Q_{r,-})\le C a^2b^2r^4(9/2)^r\) for every \(r\ge2\), and the full graph sum \(H^2(\int P_\vartheta^{\otimes n}d\Pi_+,\int P_\vartheta^{\otimes n}d\Pi_-)\le Cn^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2\), without support deletion, conditioning on a favorable occupancy event, or Poissonization without an exact reduction.
statements.justification: This is the load-bearing new proof object: one-observation cancellation alone does not control a shared-prior product likelihood.
statements.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE deletes transition-region support, while RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009SemiparametricMinimax requires partition-local perturbations; neither covers overlapping smooth frames under exact uniform support.
statements.consumer: A successful component certificate is reusable for nonlinear-functional lower bounds whenever full random-design support prevents partition-local cancellation.

statements.statement: There exist constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\), depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), such that for every \(n\ge2\), \[c\rho_n\le R_n\le C\rho_n,\qquad \rho_n=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}.\] The upper bound is attained by \(\widehat\tau_n(0)\), and the lower bound is over the same singleton exact-uniform, bounded-overlap, Bernoulli class through genuine fixed-\(n\) product laws. The theorem establishes that the nuisance-dominated candidate from KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE persists in this exact-uniform boundary experiment, which is not covered by its perforated-support lower witness.
statements.justification: The theorem determines the exact-uniform minimax order and closes the specific support gap left by the published lower experiment.
statements.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE proves the candidate exponent on a density-qualified model whose displayed hard laws have perforated local support; it does not prove this lower bound after fixing \(P_X\) to exact uniformity.
statements.consumer: The result tells users whether learning rough propensity and outcome regressions imposes an unavoidable pointwise CATE penalty even under a benign known design.

statements.statement: Under \(S<S_{\star}\), \(\eta<\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), and therefore \(R_n/\rho_n^{\mathrm{or}}\asymp n^{\gamma/(2\gamma+d)-\eta}\to\infty\). Hence no parameter tuple in the stated strict below-elbow regime attains the same-class supplied-propensity benchmark. At the sanity-check boundary \(S=S_{\star}\), the two exponents coincide and reduce to \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\) without a logarithmic multiplier.
statements.justification: The rate comparison turns the minimax theorem into an exact answer about when nuisance learning destroys oracle pointwise precision.
statements.gap: The oracle elbow appears in KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE, but its necessity on the exact-uniform subclass requires the new same-class converse.
statements.consumer: The classification supplies the decision-facing phase boundary for interpreting pointwise precision in R-learner and causal-forest workflows.

sampling_model.design: The known law \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\) has exact full support.
sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from one law \(P\in\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator knows \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L\) and the uniform design law, but not \(g_P,\mu_{0,P},\tau_P\); it uses deterministic localization and a finite projection correction rather than oracle nuisance inputs.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_n(0)=\operatorname{clip}_{[-3/4,3/4]}\{v(0)^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Q_n^{-1}\widetilde R_n\}\) on the nonsingular branch, with \(R_n\asymp\rho_n=n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}\)
target_estimand: \(\tau_P(0)=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=0]\), interpreted as the unique continuous version

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 give the nuisance-elbow pointwise CATE rate and a localized higher-order R-learner, while Appendix B.8 matches the bounds on a known density whose local support is a union of separated cubes.
Theorem 2.1 bounds the affinity of two convex mixtures of product measures under a measurable partition and coordinate-local perturbations.
Theorems 3--5 establish matched local and global conditional-variance rates under random design using local U-statistics and coupled lower laws.
Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 give local-polynomial R-learner upper rates with deterministic smoothness-dependent tuning under known-density conditions.
The paper proves a quasi-oracle error bound for an R-learner under sufficient nuisance accuracy rather than a rough-nuisance pointwise minimax converse.

tldr: A smooth pointwise CATE can be statistically easier than its propensity and outcome regressions, but the known minimax converse below the nuisance elbow uses a covariate density with holes at bump transitions. This proposal fixes the covariate law to the exact known uniform distribution and asks whether the same pure-power rate survives. The proposed lower experiment uses smooth overlapping frames and correlated signs whose one-observation mixtures cancel exactly; conditioning on all covariates converts the shared-sign dependence into sparse geometric components, and a mixed-derivative affinity bound plus spanning-tree enumeration controls the full fixed-\(n\) mixture. Paired with a total finite projection estimator, the result would prove \(R_n\asymp n^{-1/(1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2(\alpha+\beta)))}\) with no logarithmic factor and show that oracle pointwise precision is unattainable throughout the strict below-elbow regime.

project_justification.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE supplies the candidate below-elbow rate and higher-order estimator, but its displayed hard laws remove covariate mass from nuisance-bump transition regions. A lower bound over that larger density model does not imply the same bound after fixing the design to exact uniformity, and the partition-local theorem of RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009SemiparametricMinimax does not apply verbatim to overlapping smooth frames.
project_justification.niche: Exact known uniform design is simultaneously the cleanest upper-bound setting and the setting in which the published support-deletion cancellation is illegal. The unresolved object is therefore a same-class fixed-\(n\) product-mixture converse, rather than a new upper exponent or another oracle inequality.
project_justification.fill: The paper develops a correlated-sign smooth-frame prior and conditions on the observed covariates to factor its likelihood over sparse overlap components. A uniform component Hellinger inequality and random-geometric spanning-tree sum yield the missing nuisance-rate lower bound, while an explicit clipped projection U-statistic supplies the matching total upper bound.

related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE is the closest comparator: its Theorems 1--2 derive the same candidate exponent and higher-order local-polynomial architecture, while its lower proof and Appendix B.8 use a density supported on separated flat-top cells; Theorem 2 here asks whether that nuisance-dominated rate persists in the distinct singleton exact-uniform boundary experiment. RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009SemiparametricMinimax provides the two-mixture affinity theorem, but its first proof step is a deterministic partition with coordinate-local perturbations, whereas the present shared frames require factorization by random overlap components. ShenGaoWittenHan2020Variance supplies the closest random-design nonlinear-functional analogy: its conditional-variance lower proof controls repeated occupancy in local cells, motivating the treatment of non-singleton sign components. Kennedy2023DRCATE and NieWager2021RLearner explain why CATE estimation can approach an oracle regression problem under sufficient nuisance accuracy; they do not establish necessity on the rough exact-uniform class. RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2008HOIF motivates the finite projection and quadratic U-statistic correction. WagerAthey2018CausalForests is an application-facing consumer rather than a rate comparator: the theorem is a benchmark for \(\texttt{causal\_forest}\) and R-learner workflows, not a claim that an existing forest attains the bound.
technical_internal_limitation: The smooth-frame normalization, all-order H\"older bounds, uniform component derivative envelope, and inherited projection-risk calculation must each be checked independently. Exact singleton cancellation is insufficient by itself; any shared-sign term that survives outside non-singleton graph components, or any component constant growing faster than the sparse graph sum absorbs, kills the proposed converse.
honest_scope: The novelty-bearing claim is the full-support fixed-\(n\) lower bound. The upper exponent and nuisance elbow are inherited from the KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE architecture and are included to close the exact class with a total estimator. The proposal does not treat unknown design density, \(\kappa>0\) local overlap, adaptive tuning, confidence intervals, integrated loss, or performance of existing causal forests. As a sanity reduction, at \(S=S_{\star}\) the proposed exponent equals the classical oracle exponent \(\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\) without a logarithm.

seed_details.question: Does the published below-elbow pointwise CATE rate remain sharp when the covariate law is fixed to the exact known uniform distribution for every sample size?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace support deletion at nuisance-bump transitions by a smooth squared frame with shared signs, then replace deterministic partition locality by conditional factorization over random overlap components.

seed_details.red_team: The result is immediate from Kennedy et al. because their lower model contains the uniform density.
seed_details.rebuttal: A minimax lower bound over a larger density class does not transfer to a singleton subclass, and their displayed least-favorable laws have perforated rather than exact-uniform support.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The smoothness-dependent tuning equations and Discussion were read; Liu et al. Theorem 2.2 and its Lepski selection rule were opened as the method exemplar.
seed_details.question: What logarithmic price is necessary for a data-only selector adapting jointly to unknown propensity, regression, and CATE smoothness across the nuisance elbow?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the one-dimensional Lepski order over projection rank by comparisons on a two-dimensional localization-rank grid whose variance degeneracy changes across the elbow.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The higher-order estimator, bias-variance decomposition, and Discussion statement that distribution theory remains open were read together with the higher-order influence-function interval blueprint.
seed_details.question: Can one construct honest pointwise intervals whose worst-case expected length matches the below-elbow exact-uniform minimax rate?

seed_details.red_team: A Wald interval follows immediately from the risk-optimal estimator.

seed_details.anchor_opened: The localized quadratic estimator and variance proposition were read; Robins et al. on asymptotic normality of growing-kernel quadratic estimators was searched as the destination method.

novelty_justification: Theorem 1 of KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE gives the candidate nuisance-dominated exponent over a broad bounded-density model, and Theorem 2 gives the localized higher-order upper architecture. Its proof makes the squared nuisance perturbation equal the target bump by putting covariate mass only on flat bump tops; Appendix B.8 consequently matches upper and lower bounds on a known density whose local support is a union of separated cubes. The strict new delta is not the rate formula, the elbow, or the estimator idea. It is a lower bound after restricting the experiment to the singleton law \(P_X=\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\), proved for the actual fixed-\(n\) product mixture without deleting transition regions. RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009SemiparametricMinimax cannot subsume this delta because Theorem 2.1 assumes a partition on which each perturbation depends on one coordinate. The proposed smooth frames overlap, so their first factorization step fails. The replacement object is a component affinity inequality: condition on all covariates, factor by disjoint sign sets across overlap-graph components, make singleton components agree exactly, bound every remaining component by a mixed derivative, and sum them through sparse random-geometric spanning trees. ShenGaoWittenHan2020Variance confirms that repeated-cell occupancy is the right neighboring geometry but treats a Gaussian conditional-variance experiment and does not provide the Bernoulli joint-cell cancellation. Searches through September 2026 located no closer paper subsuming this exact target--method pair.

Revival of banked downgraded parent stat_cate_local_overlap_nuisance_frontier (v1), targeting its exact-uniform bounded-overlap converse that remained open. This attempt uses a joint-cell correlated-prior construction and sparse latent-sign graph component control of the full fixed-n mixture likelihood. The parent already tried smooth overlapping frames; the new ingredient is the component affinity and random-geometric-graph bound that replaces the failed partition-local transfer. Resolve the same-class below-elbow minimax rate with a matching total estimator; the rate answer remains open for independent verification. The parent all-kappa oracle theorem and unmatched upper bracket alone do not discharge this kernel. MODEL: For every fixed d>=1, alpha>0, beta>0, gamma>beta, L>=4 with S=alpha+beta<d*gamma/(2*gamma+d), observe n>=2 iid (X,A,Y). X has exactly the known uniform law on [0,1]^d. A|X=x is Bernoulli(g(x)/4), with g in H^alpha(L), 1<=g<=2. Y|(X=x,A=a) is Bernoulli(mu_a(x)), mu0 in H^beta(L), tau=mu1-mu0 in H^gamma(L), and 1/8<=mu0,mu1<=7/8. H^s(L) bounds derivatives through m=ceil(s)-1 by L and the order-m derivatives have (s-m)-Holder seminorm <=L under the sup norm. No smoothness of the marginal outcome mean is assumed. The estimator knows d,alpha,beta,gamma,L and uniform design, but not g,mu0,tau. Target is the unique continuous version tau(0); conditional exchangeability and consistency provide the causal interpretation. This is precisely the parent kappa=0 subproblem, preserving its exact-support restriction. KERNEL: Determine the sharp order of R_n=inf_T sup_P E_P|T(O_1,...,O_n)-tau_P(0)| over all Borel data-only estimators on the exact model above, for every stated fixed parameter tuple and all n>=2. Deliver an explicit deterministic rate rho_n (including any logarithmic factors), constants 0<c<=C<infinity depending only on the fixed parameters, c*rho_n<=R_n<=C*rho_n, and a total finite computable attaining estimator. Resolve whether the published candidate n^(-1/(1+d/(2gamma)+d/(2S))) is sharp on exact uniform support or supply a sharper matched replacement; the answer is open, not imposed. Characterize when the same-class oracle benchmark n^(-gamma/(2gamma+d)) remains attainable in this below-published-elbow regime. The required lower bound must concern fixed-n iid product laws in this exact full-support Bernoulli class. A conditional or Poissonized proof must prove a valid reduction back to that experiment. COMPUTATION: Use the parent finite projection U-statistic/local polynomial estimator if its rate is matched; if the class yields a faster rate, give an explicit finite projection or higher-order correction estimator with deterministic tuning, singular-matrix fallback and clipping. Frame/likelihood calculations for a lower bound are proof mechanics, not model assumptions. CONSUMER: The parent names the grf causal_forest/R-learner workflow for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects from observational data with learned propensity/outcome regressions. This theorem tells users when nuisance learning imposes an unavoidable pointwise precision penalty even under benign known covariate design, or whether that penalty is avoidable. It is a precision benchmark, not a claim that existing forests attain it; no application is changed from the parent. PRIOR ART: The parent receipts say the published higher-order upper rate already applies to exact known uniform design, but the perforated-support lower laws do not. The target is the missing full-support fixed-n converse or a sharper matched same-class answer. Sparse latent-sign component control is the presolved replacement for the failed partition-local affinity argument; no new literature review is claimed. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolver derives a full-support Bernoulli lower family using a smooth squared partition of unity and correlated signs, with a deterministic macro contrast and exact one-observation mixture cancellation. Conditional on the observed covariates, connect observations whose local frames share a sign. Product mixtures factor over components, singleton components agree, and a mixed-derivative bound controls each remaining component by a²b² times a polynomial and exponential in its size. A spanning-tree count gives a total fixed-n squared Hellinger bound of order n² h^d ell^d a²b². Below the nuisance elbow, n ell^d is small at the proposed tuning, yielding the missing nuisance-rate converse without deleting support. Root separately checked rational cell normalization, shared-coefficient mixture leakage, disjoint-component cancellation, overlapping pair/triple examples, and unequal-smoothness rate exponents. These finite checks do not prove the analytic theorem.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify the smooth-frame support and Hölder estimates, component mixed-derivative constants, geometric-graph counting, and the inherited upper estimator; the presolver reports an analytic closure, not a certified theorem.
EARLY KILL TEST: On d=1, alpha=beta=1/8, gamma=1, verify the full fixed-n component factorization and affinity estimate at ell proportional to n^(-8/7); stop if an uncancelled singleton or macro-scale leakage term survives.
